clue.text: Run away! I'm with a celebrity on vacation to get credibility

indicators.note: a vacated building has been emptied, so only the word's two ends are left standing

blocks.note: 'leg it' is slang for running off
taken as written
taken as written
the word with its whole middle cleared out

explanation.surface: Someone flees a celebrity they are holidaying with, hoping to look respectable.
explanation.walkthrough: LEG IT + IM + A + CY gives LEGITIMACY; 'with' simply joins the first two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Legitimacy is the quality of being accepted as genuine and lawful, which is close kin to believability.

clue.text: Hold out fake foot

blocks.note: first meaning: to endure or keep going
second meaning: the shoemaker's wooden model of a foot

explanation.walkthrough: A last is the foot-shaped block a cobbler builds a shoe around, hence a fake foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to survive or endure a stretch of time, and the noun is a cobbler's wooden form.

clue.text: Almost castrate setter

indicators.note: almost means falling just short, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to geld is to castrate an animal

explanation.surface: A grim threat against the crossword compiler, stopping just short of mutilation.
explanation.walkthrough: GELD loses its D. 'Setter' looks like the crossword's compiler, but here it is anything that sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair gel or a culinary gel is a substance that sets firm, so it is literally something that sets.

clue.text: Walk rated abysmal

indicators.note: something abysmal is a terrible mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A judge's verdict on a model's catwalk performance: very poor.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread is to step or walk along, as in treading a path.

clue.text: Mother hides Agent Purple

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside you, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: an informal word for mother
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spy codenamed Agent Purple is being sheltered by his mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agent Purple' reads as a spy's codename, but Purple stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is a purplish-red colour, so it is a shade of purple.

clue.text: Company boss at last to fire old Russian

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter only of the word before it

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for a company
the final letter of the word
to sack is to dismiss from a job

explanation.surface: A company chief finally decides to dismiss an elderly Russian employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like shooting; it is dismissal. The Cossacks were a Russian warrior people of the steppes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cossacks were a historic people of southern Russia and Ukraine, famed horsemen of the Tsarist era.

clue.text: Confirmation nothing escapes teacher

indicators.note: whatever escapes gets out and is gone, so that letter leaves the word

blocks.note: proof confirms that something is true
zero, shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: Evidence that nothing gets past the schoolteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: PROOF drops one O to leave PROF.
explanation.definitionFit: Prof is the informal short form of professor, a university teacher.

clue.text: Cycling around external path

indicators.note: cycling round means the letters rotate, the last one coming back to the front

blocks.note: outer means on the outside

explanation.surface: A cyclist takes the outer ring road rather than the city centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The final R of OUTER moves to the front. 'Cycling' paints a bike ride but signals rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is the way or course taken to get somewhere, much like a path.

clue.text: Warning shots to protect small expanses of trees

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround it, so the short piece goes inside

blocks.note: the golfer's shout to warn of an incoming ball
tries are attempts or shots at something
the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Warning shots are fired to defend little patches of woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: A golfer shouts 'Fore!' to warn people standing in the ball's path.
explanation.definitionFit: Forestry can mean a wooded area itself, so forestries are wide stretches of woodland.

clue.text: Six cardinals in Rome meeting a nationalist with no military involvement

blocks.note: six Roman numerals in a row: one hundred, one, five, one, fifty, one
taken as written
the abbreviation for nationalist

explanation.surface: A conclave of cardinals in Rome meets a political firebrand, without any soldiers present.
explanation.walkthrough: The cardinals are cardinal numbers, not churchmen: C, I, V, I, L and I are each Roman numerals. CIVILI + A + N.
explanation.definitionFit: Civilian as an adjective describes people or activity outside the armed forces, not involving soldiers.

clue.text: Very, very half-cut nurses left to clear up

indicators.note: half-cut means half has been lopped off, so only the first part of the word survives
to nurse something is to hold it close, so one piece is cradled inside

blocks.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
taken as written before being cut
the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone drunk tends to a patient, and the job is to tidy up afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-cut is British slang for drunk, but here it halves the second 'very'.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear up a puzzle or mystery is to work it out, which is what solving means.

clue.text: Start to gently creep in Boston, reportedly to get local product of distillation

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter alone
reportedly means as heard, and in Boston means said in that city's r-dropping accent

blocks.note: the opening letter
a crude name for a sycophantic creep, said with a Boston accent that drops the final r

explanation.surface: Instructions to sneak quietly about a Boston bar to get some home-distilled spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: A Bostonian says the slang for a toady as 'ass-licka', which is how 'a-sliquor' sounds. Gas liquor is the watery by-product of the local gasworks.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas liquor is the ammonia-rich liquid left when coal was distilled to make town gas at the local gasworks.

clue.text: In Spain, I'd rashly written about Mediterranean island

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows
about means turned round, so the concealed letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the letters running from the end of Spain to the start of rashly

explanation.surface: A Spanish writer has dashed off a careless piece about an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The island is in the letters 'spAIN I'D RAShly', read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardinia is the large Italian island in the Mediterranean, west of the mainland and south of Corsica.

clue.text: Collection of photographs of a large bottom

blocks.note: taken as written
the clothing-size abbreviation for large
informal British word for the backside

explanation.surface: Snapshots of an ample backside gathered in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a book of pages for keeping photographs together.

clue.text: Components of Times cryptic

indicators.note: a cryptic version is a disguised one, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzle-lover's remark about the parts that make up a rival newspaper's crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times cryptic' reads as the rival paper's crossword; cryptic is really the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Items are individual parts or elements of a whole, much like the parts making up a set.

clue.text: Sadat, possibly, supporting unlawful act in conflict

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporter holds up from below, so this piece goes beneath the other

blocks.note: a crime breaks the law
Anwar Sadat was President of Egypt; possibly marks him as one example of the name

explanation.surface: The Egyptian president is backing an illegal act during a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadat' leads the eye to Egypt, but it is his first name that is needed, placed under CRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean War of 1853 to 1856 was the conflict pitting Russia against Britain, France and the Ottomans.

clue.text: Nearly execute beautiful Italian getting disease

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the word's final letter is lost

blocks.note: to run a program or plan is to execute it
the Italian for beautiful

explanation.surface: A lovely Italian woman, almost put to death, falls ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Execute' suggests killing; it is the sense of carrying out a task. RU + BELLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubella, also called German measles, is a contagious viral infection marked by a rash.

clue.text: Laxative in toilets upset Frenchman

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: loo is informal British for toilet
a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is unwell in the toilets after a dose of laxative.
explanation.walkthrough: LOOS + RENE written upwards (ENER).
explanation.definitionFit: A loosener is something that loosens the bowels, an informal name for a purgative.

clue.text: Needleworker's fancy trinket

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are worked into a new pattern

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A seamstress shows off her ornamental bauble.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay rather than marking possession.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who knits works with needles and yarn, so is a kind of needle craftsperson.

clue.text: Statement lifting the lid over figure of speech

indicators.note: lifting off a lid removes the top, and in a down clue the top is the first letter
over means turned over, so the remaining letters run the other way

blocks.note: a report is a formal statement

explanation.surface: A press release reveals the truth behind a turn of phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: REPORT loses its first letter to EPORT, which is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figurative or metaphorical use of a word, the technical term for such a figure.

clue.text: Huge match regularly stopped by missiles?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
something stopped by an object has it plugged inside, like a cork in a bottle

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters
short for ammunition, which includes missiles

explanation.surface: A massive fixture is halted by objects thrown from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that missiles are only one kind of ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoth as an adjective means enormous, from the giant extinct elephant.

clue.text: Drugs leading lady

blocks.note: first of two drugs
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A star actress is caught with narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'Drugs' supplies two of them: HEROIN and E, ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A heroine is the principal female character of a story or the lead actress in a play.

clue.text: Prisoner's only comfort

blocks.note: short for convict
sole means only, as in 'sole survivor'

explanation.surface: A jailbird's one source of solace.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'has', so the prisoner has sole beside him: CON + SOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To console someone is to comfort them in grief or disappointment; both are verbs.

clue.text: Most wary actors in play concealing gripes, oddly

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, the first, third and fifth letters
to conceal is to hold something hidden within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the cast is the set of actors in a production
letters one, three and five

explanation.surface: Performers in a show are hiding their complaints and being very guarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Cagey means guarded and reluctant to give information, so the superlative is the most cautious.

clue.text: American and European mostly get on together

indicators.note: mostly means all but a little, so the last letter is removed

blocks.note: the abbreviation for American
a Greek is one kind of European

explanation.surface: An American and a European largely see eye to eye.
explanation.walkthrough: A + GREE(K).
explanation.definitionFit: People who agree share the same view, which is what it is to get along with one another.

clue.text: Unwilling to go forward and put pig in new home?

blocks.note: first meaning: an old word for restive or balky, used of a horse
second meaning: read as ..., to house a pig in a sty once more

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful invented verb: RE (again) plus STY (a pig's home), flagged by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Resty is an archaic adjective for a horse that is stubborn and refuses to move on, like restive.

clue.text: Express terrible regret about Iceland

indicators.note: something terrible is in a dreadful state, so the letters are mangled
about means going round, so the jumbled letters wrap the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
IS is the international code for Iceland

explanation.surface: Someone apologises deeply over an Icelandic matter, perhaps the banking collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like an instruction to the solver but is the definition: to register an emotion is to show it.
explanation.definitionFit: To register a feeling, such as surprise or a protest, is to show or voice it outwardly.

clue.text: Growl "Get knotted!"

blocks.note: first meaning: an angry baring of teeth
second meaning: to become tangled

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get knotted!' is a rude British brush-off, which fits the growl, but here it is literal: to become tangled.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog snarls by growling with bared teeth, and hair or rope snarls up when tangled.

clue.text: German woman helping entertaining hosts

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so the words before it hold the letters within them

blocks.note: the tail of the first word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A German lady lends a hand while her guests are entertained.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'helpING Entertaining'; 'entertaining' itself looks like the signal, but it is part of the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: Inge is a common German girl's name, short for Ingeborg or Ingrid.

clue.text: Refuse offer of pap rub from Spooner

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds trade places

blocks.note: pap is a soft paste and to rub is to wipe

explanation.surface: Turning down a deal on a soft ointment massage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse offer' reads as declining a deal, but it is 'refuse off-er': something that carries refuse off.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipe from a sink or bath takes dirty water and rubbish away, so it removes refuse.

clue.text: Order foreign government to replace base

indicators.note: one thing replacing another takes its place, so a letter is swapped out

blocks.note: alien means from another country
the abbreviation for government
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A command for an overseas regime to take over a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: In ALIEN, G takes the place of E. The mathematical constant e is called the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: To align things is to put them in a straight line or proper arrangement, setting them in order.

clue.text: One's charged celebrity to have head shaved

indicators.note: shaving the head takes off the top, and in a down clue the top is the first letter

blocks.note: a lion is a celebrated person, as in a literary lion

explanation.surface: A famous person, charged by police, gets their head shaved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's charged' sounds like a court case; it means one that is electrically charged.
explanation.definitionFit: An ion is an atom or molecule carrying an electric charge from gaining or losing electrons.

clue.text: Beams, as pay increase announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a raise is an increase in salary

explanation.surface: Workers smile broadly as a salary rise is declared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beams' looks like smiles but means shafts of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays are narrow shafts of light, which are also called beams.

clue.text: Perhaps guinea pig still with time to move east in epidemic

indicators.note: in an across answer east is rightwards, so that letter shifts one place along

blocks.note: a guinea pig is one example of a pet
the still of the night is its silence
the abbreviation T, already in the first piece, is what moves

explanation.surface: A pet guinea pig is still, then time shifts east during an outbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: PET + SILENCE gives PETSILENCE; the T then moves one place right to give PESTILENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestilence is a deadly widespread disease, the old word for a plague sweeping through a population.
